source.note: Official WCS student calendar. This is the pacing anchor for EVERY Social Studies Hack course pacing guide — do not pace to a generic 180-day calendar.

key_dates.label: Constitution Day observed (students in school)
key_dates.instructional_hook: Legally observed; natural anchor for Government GC.01-GC.09 and any Constitution content across courses.

key_dates.label: End of First Quarter (44 grading days)
End of First Semester (half day, 39 grading days)
End of Third Quarter (46 grading days)
Last Day for Students (half day) / End of Second Semester (48 grading days)

late_start_6_12.note: 6-12 Late Start days shorten instruction by 45 min — pacing must not assume a full period on these days.

inclement_weather.note: Up to 10 weather days are stockpiled and not made up; beyond 10, makeup days come from Mid-Winter Break, PD day, Spring Holiday, then Spring Break. Pacing should carry a small buffer rather than assume all 177 days are protected.

pacing_rules: Anchor every course's unit pacing to the semester + quarter boundaries above (Q1 end Oct 9, S1 end Dec 18, Q3 end Mar 12, S2 end May 27).

A full-year course (US History, World History, Government) must fit its units + assessments + review into 177 instructional days, leaving buffer for the ~10 stockpiled weather days and the 27 late-start days.
Do NOT schedule a summative unit assessment on a half day (Aug 10, Dec 18, May 27) or the day before a multi-day break.
Place EOC/TCAP review in the window feeding the state testing calendar (see WCS Assessment Page); leave the last 2-3 weeks of S2 for review + testing.
Constitution Day (Sep 17) and Election Day proximity (Nov 3) are civic hooks — Government pacing should land the relevant standards near these dates where feasible.
